title: A thread-safe word counter
description:
Write a class `WordCounter` that several threads can feed at the same time:

- `add_text(text)` splits `text` on whitespace, lower-cases each word, strips the characters `.,!?;:"'()` from both ends, skips words that become empty, and counts the rest.
- `count(word)` returns how many times the word (any case) has been added.
- `most_common(n)` returns the `n` most frequent `(word, count)` pairs, highest count first, ties in alphabetical order.
- Every method must be safe to call from many threads at once: guard the shared counts with a `threading.Lock`.

Then write `count_in_parallel(texts, workers=4)` that creates one `WordCounter`, feeds it all `texts` from a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, and returns it.

solution.solution.py:
import threading
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

PUNCTUATION = ".,!?;:\"'()"


class WordCounter:
    def __init__(self):
        self._counts = Counter()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def add_text(self, text):
        words = [w.lower().strip(PUNCTUATION) for w in text.split()]
        local = Counter(w for w in words if w)
        with self._lock:
            self._counts.update(local)

    def count(self, word):
        with self._lock:
            return self._counts[word.lower()]

    def most_common(self, n):
        with self._lock:
            items = list(self._counts.items())
        items.sort(key=lambda pair: (-pair[1], pair[0]))
        return items[:n]


def count_in_parallel(texts, workers=4):
    counter = WordCounter()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        list(pool.map(counter.add_text, texts))
    return counter

hints: Do the slow part (splitting and cleaning) **outside** the lock, into a local `Counter`, then hold the lock only for the short `update` of the shared one. That keeps threads from waiting for each other.
`str.strip(chars)` removes any of the given characters from both ends. Sort with `key=lambda pair: (-pair[1], pair[0])` for "highest count, then alphabetical".
